entry.name: js
entry.description: Exposes the Javascript language (ECMAScript 5) and some Max specific extensions. The js object can be instantiated with a javascript filename or with numerical arguments to specify the number of outlets and inlets respectively. The default number of outlets and inlets are both 1.

arguments.name: filename
arguments.description: Specifies the name of a text file to be used as the Javascript source. If no argument is specified, it will not initially have any Javascript associated with it. You can still open a text window and edit and save the Javascript source, but unless you recreate the object with the saved source filename as an argument, the file will not be used when a patch containing theobject is loaded.

arguments.name: inlets-outlets
arguments.description: If no filename is present as an argument, the number of inlets and outlets is specified. If one int argument is present, the number of desired outlets is specified. If two int arguments are present, the first number specifies the number of outlets and the second number specifies the number of inlets.

arguments.name: jsarguments
arguments.description: Following the optional filename or number of outlets and inlets, any symbols or numbers can be entered that will be assigned to the Javascript variable jsarguments. jsarguments[0] is the filename entered, and jsarguments[1] is the first typed-in argument following the filename. The Javascript expression jsarguments.length will be one more than the number of typed-in arguments

messages.name: anything
messages.description: Invokes the function with the message name, assigning the message arguments to the arguments to the function. For example, if the object has a function named xyz defined, the messagewould invoke the xyz function with arguments 1 2 and 3.

messages.name: autowatch
messages.digest: Watch for changes in the source file
messages.description: The message, followed by a 1, turns on file watching for the Javascript source file. When file watching is on, the file is recompiled automatically when it is modified. This allows you to use an external editor for your Javascript file. When you save the file, theobject will notice.turns off file watching.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Send a bang to the Javascript
messages.description: Invokes the function named bang if defined.

messages.name: compile
messages.description: Recompiles the current file. If followed by a symbol, will load, compile, and set the currently loaded Javascript file to be the file specified by the symbol argument.

messages.name: delprop
messages.description: The word, followed by a name, deletes the named property.

messages.name: editfontsize
messages.digest: Change the editing window's font size
messages.description: Changes the font-size of the text used in the editing window which contains the object's Javascript source file.

messages.name: float
messages.description: Invokes the function named msg_float if defined.

messages.name: getprop
messages.description: The word, followed by a name, outputs the value of the property name stored in the object out the left outlet.

messages.name: int
messages.description: Invokes the function named msg_int if defined.

messages.name: loadbang
messages.description: Invokes the function named loadbang if defined. This message is sent when the file is loaded.

messages.name: open
messages.digest: Open a window for Javascript editing
messages.description: Opens the text window where the object's Javascript source file can be edited.

messages.name: setprop
messages.description: The word, followed by name and one or more names or numbers, sets the named property to what follows the name. For example, after sending setpropto aobject. the xyz property would have a value of the list 1 2 3.

messages.name: statemessage
messages.description: Allows for the testing of messages passed to functions within the Javascript source file.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: Closes the text window where the object's Javascript source file is edited.
